subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Atomic structure and the periodic table

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: A proton carries a relative charge of +1, balanced by the -1 charge of the electron.

questions.q: What is the relative mass of an electron?
questions.explain: An electron has a very small relative mass of about 1/1835 compared with a proton or neutron.

questions.q: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom concentrated?
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons in the tiny central nucleus account for nearly all of an atom's mass.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element tells you the number of which particle?
questions.explain: The atomic (proton) number equals the number of protons, which defines the element.

questions.q: Two isotopes of the same element must have the same number of protons but a different number of what?
questions.explain: Isotopes have identical proton numbers but different numbers of neutrons, giving different mass numbers.

questions.q: The alpha particle scattering experiment provided evidence for which idea?
options: Most of the atom is empty space with a small, dense, positive nucleus
Electrons are spread evenly through a positive 'pudding'
questions.explain: Deflection of some alpha particles showed the atom's mass and positive charge are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

questions.q: Which model of the atom described a ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it?
questions.explain: Thomson's plum pudding model pictured negative electrons embedded in a cloud of positive charge.

questions.q: Chlorine is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
An atom has the electronic configuration 2,8,1. Which element is it?
questions.explain: The configuration 2,8,1 contains 11 electrons, so the neutral atom is sodium (atomic number 11).

questions.q: Mendeleev arranged the elements in his periodic table primarily in order of what, leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
questions.explain: Mendeleev ordered elements by relative atomic mass and left gaps that predicted undiscovered elements.

questions.q: Why do elements in the same group of the periodic table have similar chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same relative atomic mass
questions.explain: Chemical behaviour depends on outer-shell electrons, and elements in a group share the same number of them.

questions.q: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases with full outer shells?
questions.explain: Group 0 (the noble gases) have full outer shells, making them very unreactive.

questions.q: An ionic bond is best described as what?
options: The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
The attraction between two neutral molecules
questions.explain: Ionic bonding is the strong electrostatic force of attraction between positive and negative ions.

questions.q: When a metal reacts with a non-metal to form an ionic compound, what happens to the electrons?
options: Electrons are transferred from the metal to the non-metal
Electrons are shared equally between the atoms
Electrons become delocalised throughout the structure
Electrons are transferred from the non-metal to the metal
questions.explain: The metal loses outer electrons to form positive ions and the non-metal gains them to form negative ions.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed by what?
options: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
The attraction between ions and delocalised electrons
The loss of electrons by both atoms
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when two non-metal atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

questions.q: Which description best fits the structure of a metal?
options: A lattice of positive ions surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons
A lattice of oppositely charged ions
Small molecules held by weak forces
A giant structure of atoms sharing electron pairs
questions.explain: Metallic bonding involves a regular lattice of positive ions held together by delocalised electrons.

questions.q: Magnesium forms Mg2+ ions and chlorine forms Cl- ions. What is the formula of magnesium chloride?
questions.explain: Two Cl- ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge of one Mg2+ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: Why can metals conduct electricity?
options: They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move
They contain ions that move through the solid
They share electrons in fixed covalent bonds
They have full outer electron shells
questions.explain: Delocalised electrons in the metallic lattice are free to move and carry charge through the metal.

questions.q: Using relative atomic masses Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, what is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO3?
How many moles are in 40 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH (Mr = 40)?
questions.explain: Moles = mass / Mr = 40 / 40 = 1 mol.
